definition.simple: Using wind to blow away light dirt and leaves from heavy grains.
definition.academic: Winnowing is an agricultural method used to separate grain from chaff. It involves dropping the mixture from a height so that the wind blows away the lighter chaff while the heavier grains fall straight down.

examples: Using a winnowing basket (Supdi) to clean rice
Dropping wheat from a height on a breezy day

common_misconceptions: Winnowing breaks the grain from the stalk. (No, threshing does that. Winnowing only uses wind to separate them).
ai_context.tutor_hint: Ask the student what happens if you drop a handful of sand and dry leaves on a windy day. Which one blows away? The lighter leaves! That's winnowing.
